chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Monopolizing (hoarding) during abundance is for forty days, and during hardship and affliction is for three days. So whatever exceeds forty days during abundance, its owner is accursed, and whatever exceeds three days during scarcity, its owner is accursed.

key_terms.الْحُكْرَةُ: Monopoly or hoarding of goods to raise prices

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hoarding goods and price control?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential boundaries of al-hukrah (monopoly/hoarding) by distinguishing between periods of abundance and scarcity, a distinction rooted in the economic realities of early Islamic markets. The designation of the hoarder as 'accursed' (mal'un) underscores the severity of violating these temporal limits, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing artificial inflation and ensuring market fairness for the community. This ruling serves as a practical mechanism for price stabilization, linking religious obligation directly to economic justice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The monopolising during the abundance is of forty days, and during the difficulty and the affliction is of three days. So whatever is increased upon the forty days during the abundance, so its perpetrator is an accursed, and whatever is increased upon three days during the shortages, so its perpetrator is an accursed’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’

At a time when food is abundantly available, keeping food for forty days is considered hoarding, but at the time of shortages of food holding back food supplies for three days is considered hoarding. After forty days at a time when food is abundant a hoarder is condemned and at the time of scarcity of food after three days the hoarder is condemned.’”
